docs.title: UV Package Manager - Tutorial & Commands
docs.text: UV is a blazingly fast Python package and project manager written in Rust. It's designed as a drop-in replacement for pip, pip-tools, and virtualenv, but 10-100x faster.

docs.title: Why UV?
docs.text:
• Speed: 10-100x faster than pip
  • Unified tool: Replaces pip, pip-tools, virtualenv, and more
  • Reliable: Built in Rust with proper dependency resolution
  • Compatible: Works with existing Python projects and PyPI

docs.title: Install UV
docs.text:
# Using pip
pip install uv

# Using curl (recommended for system-wide install)
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Using homebrew (macOS)
brew install uv

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text: uv --version

docs.title: 1. Creating a New Project
docs.text:
# Create a new Python project
uv init my-project
cd my-project

This creates:

  • pyproject.toml - Project configuration
  • .python-version - Python version specification
  • Basic project structure

docs.title: 2. Installing Packages
docs.text:
# Install a package
uv pip install requests

# Install specific version
uv pip install requests==2.31.0

# Install multiple packages
uv pip install requests pandas numpy

# Install from requirements.txt
uv pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 3. Virtual Environments
docs.text:
# Create a virtual environment
uv venv

# Create with specific Python version
uv venv --python 3.11

# Activate the environment
# On macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate

# On Windows:
.venv\\Scripts\\activate

docs.title: Installing Packages
docs.text:
# Install package
uv pip install <package>

# Install with extras
uv pip install "fastapi[all]"

# Install editable package (development mode)
uv pip install -e .

# Install from git
uv pip install git+https://github.com/user/repo.git

# Install specific commit/branch/tag
uv pip install git+https://github.com/user/repo.git@main
uv pip install git+https://github.com/user/repo.git@v1.0.0

docs.title: Uninstalling Packages
docs.text:
# Uninstall a package
uv pip uninstall requests

# Uninstall multiple packages
uv pip uninstall requests pandas numpy

docs.title: Listing Packages
docs.text:
# List installed packages
uv pip list

# List in freeze format
uv pip freeze

# Show package details
uv pip show requests

docs.title: Upgrading Packages
docs.text:
# Upgrade a package
uv pip install --upgrade requests

# Upgrade all packages
uv pip install --upgrade -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Virtual Environment Commands
docs.text:
# Create virtual environment
uv venv

# Create with name
uv venv myenv

# Create with specific Python version
uv venv --python 3.11
uv venv --python 3.10.5

# Create without pip
uv venv --no-pip

# Use system site packages
uv venv --system-site-packages

docs.title: Generate Requirements
docs.text:
# Generate requirements.txt from current environment
uv pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Compile requirements with locked versions
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt

# Update locked requirements
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt --upgrade

docs.title: Sync Environment
docs.text:
# Sync environment to match requirements.txt exactly
uv pip sync requirements.txt

# This uninstalls packages not in requirements.txt

docs.title: Working with pyproject.toml
docs.text:
UV natively understands pyproject.toml for modern Python projects:

[project]
name = "my-project"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "requests>=2.31.0",
    "pandas>=2.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "black>=23.0",
    "ruff>=0.1.0",
]

Install project dependencies:

# Install project dependencies
uv pip install -e .

# Install with dev dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Compiling Requirements
docs.text:
requirements.in (high-level dependencies):

requests
pandas>=2.0
flask

Compile to lock all transitive dependencies:

# Compile requirements.in to requirements.txt
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt

# Upgrade packages during compilation
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt --upgrade

# Compile for specific Python version
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt --python-version 3.11

docs.title: Cache Management
docs.text:
# Show cache directory
uv cache dir

# Clean cache
uv cache clean

# Show cache size
du -sh $(uv cache dir)

docs.title: Global Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv --version Show UV version uv --help Show help message uv self update Update UV to latest version

docs.title: pip Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv pip install <pkg> Install package uv pip uninstall <pkg> Uninstall package uv pip list List installed packages uv pip freeze Output installed packages in requirements format uv pip show <pkg> Show package information uv pip check Verify installed packages have compatible dependencies uv pip compile <file> Compile requirements file with locked versions uv pip sync <file> Sync environment to requirements file

docs.title: venv Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv venv Create virtual environment uv venv <name> Create named virtual environment uv venv --python <version> Create with specific Python version

docs.title: cache Commands
docs.text: Command Description uv cache dir Show cache directory uv cache clean Clean cache

docs.title: Starting a New Project
docs.text:
# 1. Create project directory
mkdir my-project && cd my-project

# 2. Initialize project (optional)
uv init

# 3. Create virtual environment
uv venv

# 4. Activate virtual environment
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# or
.venv\\Scripts\\activate  # Windows

# 5. Install dependencies
uv pip install requests pandas numpy

# 6. Freeze requirements
uv pip freeze > requirements.txt

docs.title: Cloning an Existing Project
docs.text:
# 1. Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/user/project.git
cd project

# 2. Create virtual environment
uv venv

# 3. Activate environment
source .venv/bin/activate

# 4. Install dependencies
uv pip install -r requirements.txt

# 5. Install project in editable mode (if setup.py/pyproject.toml exists)
uv pip install -e .

docs.title: Managing Dependencies with Compile + Sync
docs.text:
# 1. Create requirements.in with high-level dependencies
echo "requests\npandas>=2.0\nflask" > requirements.in

# 2. Compile to lock versions
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt

# 3. Sync environment
uv pip sync requirements.txt

# 4. To update dependencies later
uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt --upgrade
uv pip sync requirements.txt

docs.title: Development vs Production Dependencies
docs.text:
requirements.in:

requests
flask

requirements-dev.in:

-c requirements.txt
pytest
black
ruff

Compile both:

uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt
uv pip compile requirements-dev.in -o requirements-dev.txt

docs.title: Speed Optimization
docs.text:
✅ UV is already optimized, but you can:

  • Use uv pip sync instead of uv pip install -r when possible (faster)
  • Leverage the cache - UV caches downloads automatically
  • Use --no-deps flag to skip dependency resolution if you know dependencies are satisfied

docs.title: Compatibility with pip
docs.text:
✅ Drop-in replacement: Most pip commands work with uv pip

# These are equivalent:
pip install requests
uv pip install requests

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
# Disable cache
export UV_NO_CACHE=1

# Custom cache directory
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/path/to/cache

# Set index URL
export UV_INDEX_URL=https://custom-pypi.example.com/simple

docs.title: Using with Docker
docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim

# Install UV
RUN pip install uv

# Copy requirements
COPY requirements.txt .

# Install dependencies with UV (much faster!)
RUN uv pip install --system -r requirements.txt

# Copy application
COPY . .

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Migration from pip
docs.text:
Before (pip):

pip install -r requirements.txt
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pip list

After (UV):

uv pip install -r requirements.txt
uv pip freeze > requirements.txt
uv pip list

Just add uv before pip!

docs.title: Issue: Command not found
docs.text:
# Ensure UV is in PATH
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"

# Or reinstall
pip install --upgrade uv

docs.title: Issue: Dependency conflicts
docs.text:
# Check for conflicts
uv pip check

# Use compile to see dependency tree
uv pip compile requirements.in --verbose

docs.title: Issue: Slow downloads
docs.text:
# Use a mirror
uv pip install --index-url https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple requests

# Or set permanently
export UV_INDEX_URL=https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple

docs.title: Quick Reference Card
docs.text:
# Installation
pip install uv

# Virtual environment
uv venv                          # Create
source .venv/bin/activate       # Activate (Unix)
.venv\\Scripts\\activate          # Activate (Windows)

# Install packages
uv pip install <package>         # Install
uv pip install -r requirements.txt  # From file
uv pip install -e .              # Editable mode

# Manage dependencies
uv pip list                      # List packages
uv pip freeze > requirements.txt # Save requirements
uv pip compile requirements.in   # Lock dependencies
uv pip sync requirements.txt     # Sync environment

# Update
uv pip install --upgrade <pkg>   # Upgrade package
uv self update                   # Update UV itself

# Cache
uv cache clean                   # Clear cache
uv cache dir                     # Show cache location
